followUps.function: CAN controller clock (the crystal, resonator or oscillator each controller takes)
followUps.reason: function the row names that P2 did not return: hardware/docs/IOBoard.md:169 names 'Controller clock' as a requirement row in state 'required'. IOBoard.md:111 says the CAN bit rate is exact to the controller's clock and that R2 states its tolerance. The R2 row requires R2 to state each controller's clock tolerance. P2 carries that tolerance (V26, V27) as a requirement value of the two controllers, but no entry selects the clock part. Every shortlisted controller needs one. The MCP2518FD takes a '40, 20 or 4 MHz Crystal or Ceramic Resonator' or an external clock. Its Table 7-3 bounds the OSC1 input at +/-0.5 % (DS20006027B, https://ww1.microchip.com/downloads/aemDocuments/documents/OTH/ProductDocuments/DataSheets/External-CAN-FD-Controller-with-SPI-Interface-DS20006027B.pdf, read 2026-09-29T00:47:30Z). The MCP2515 driver in the tree takes a 16 MHz crystal (IOBoard.md:169). R1 selects the RP2354B's 12 MHz crystal as a function of its own, a round 1 part.
